```{r, include = FALSE}
# The gallery is mostly ggplot2, which jacarandr only suggests, so every
# chunk runs only when ggplot2 is installed.
#
# This file is also the source of the README images: data-raw/readme-figures.R
# knits it and keeps the figures, so chunk labels double as image file names.
# Rename a chunk and the README link must change too. That script also sets
# the option below for sharper images; the vignette itself keeps them small.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.2,
  dpi = getOption("jacarandr.gallery.dpi", 96),
  eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
)
```

A few example plots made with jacarandr, each built with only ggplot2 and
its own example data, so you can copy any of them as a starting point.

## Setup

The plots share one light theme. It is ordinary ggplot2 and not part of
jacarandr.

```{r setup}
library(jacarandr)
library(ggplot2)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35",
                                   margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.caption = element_text(colour = "grey55", size = 9),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification = "left",
      legend.title = element_blank()
    )
)
```

## The palettes

```{r palette-card, fig.height = 3.6}
# Every colour as a tile: the two discrete palettes as labelled swatches and
# the two continuous palettes as smooth ramps underneath.
main <- jac_colours()
discrete <- rbind(
  data.frame(row = 4, x = 1:8, fill = unname(main),
             label = paste0(gsub("_", " ", names(main)), "\n", main)),
  data.frame(row = 3, x = 1:8, fill = jac_pal("light"),
             label = jac_pal("light"))
)
# Dark swatches get white text: CIELAB lightness below 55 counts as dark.
lightness <- grDevices::convertColor(
  t(grDevices::col2rgb(discrete$fill)) / 255, from = "sRGB", to = "Lab"
)[, "L"]
discrete$ink <- ifelse(lightness < 55, "white", "grey10")

ramp_x <- seq(0.5, 8.5, length.out = 101)
ramps <- rbind(
  data.frame(row = 2, x = ramp_x, fill = jac_pal("seq", n = 101)),
  data.frame(row = 1, x = ramp_x, fill = jac_pal("div", n = 101))
)

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = ramps, aes(x, row, fill = fill),
            width = 8 / 100, height = 0.82) +
  geom_tile(data = discrete, aes(x, row, fill = fill),
            width = 0.94, height = 0.82) +
  geom_text(data = discrete, aes(x, row, label = label, colour = ink),
            size = 3, lineheight = 0.95) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.3, y = 4:1, hjust = 1, colour = "grey30",
           label = c("main", "light", "seq", "div"), fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.4, 8.5), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "jacarandr",
       subtitle = paste("Jacaranda in bloom, with flame tree, wattle,",
                        "gum leaves and paperbark")) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey35",
                                     margin = margin(b = 8)),
        plot.margin = margin(12, 12, 12, 12))
```

## Highlighting one bar

Use `jac_colours()` to pick colours by name. Here a single jacaranda bar
stands out against neutral paperbark.

```{r bars-highlight}
counts <- as.data.frame(table(class = mpg$class))
counts$class <- reorder(counts$class, counts$Freq)
counts$highlight <- counts$class == "suv"

ggplot(counts, aes(Freq, class, fill = highlight)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), hjust = -0.3, colour = "grey30", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(jac_colours("paperbark", "jacaranda")),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(title = "SUVs lead the fleet",
       subtitle = "Number of models by vehicle class",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Data: ggplot2::mpg") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Proportions

The first few `"main"` colours are always the most distinct, so they suit
stacked bars well.

```{r bars-stacked}
ggplot(mpg, aes(y = class, fill = drv)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_jac_d(labels = c("4" = "Four-wheel", f = "Front", r = "Rear")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x * 100, "%"),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Drive train by vehicle class",
       subtitle = "Share of models in each class",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Data: ggplot2::mpg") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(5.5, 16, 5.5, 5.5))
```

## Grouped bars

With eight groups, the full `"main"` palette comes into play. Ordering the
groups by value keeps the bars in each year easy to compare.

```{r bars-grouped}
# The eight makes with the most models, and their mean highway economy.
makes <- names(sort(table(mpg$manufacturer), decreasing = TRUE))[1:8]
economy <- aggregate(hwy ~ manufacturer + year,
                     data = subset(mpg, manufacturer %in% makes),
                     FUN = mean)
# Order the makes from most to least efficient in 2008.
latest <- economy[economy$year == 2008, ]
economy$manufacturer <- factor(
  economy$manufacturer,
  levels = latest$manufacturer[order(latest$hwy, decreasing = TRUE)]
)
# Capitalise the names for display ("volkswagen" -> "Volkswagen").
lv <- levels(economy$manufacturer)
levels(economy$manufacturer) <- paste0(toupper(substring(lv, 1, 1)),
                                       substring(lv, 2))

ggplot(economy, aes(factor(year), hwy, fill = manufacturer)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.85), width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_jac_d() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(title = "Volkswagen leads on the highway",
       subtitle = "Mean highway miles per gallon of the eight biggest makes",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Data: ggplot2::mpg") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
```

## Lines with direct labels

Labelling lines directly is easier to read than a legend. Here each label
takes the same colour as its line.

```{r lines}
econ <- subset(economics_long, variable %in% c("pce", "unemploy", "psavert"))
econ$variable <- factor(econ$variable,
                        levels = c("psavert", "unemploy", "pce"),
                        labels = c("Savings rate", "Unemployed", "Spending"))

# One label per line at its last value, nudged apart where lines end close
# together so the labels never overlap.
last <- econ[econ$date == max(econ$date), ]
last <- last[order(last$value01), ]
last$label_y <- last$value01
for (i in seq_len(nrow(last))[-1]) {
  last$label_y[i] <- max(last$value01[i], last$label_y[i - 1] + 0.08)
}

ggplot(econ, aes(date, value01, colour = variable)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = last, aes(y = label_y, label = variable), hjust = 0,
            nudge_x = 250, size = 3.6, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_colour_jac_d(guide = "none") +
  scale_x_date(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.16))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Half a century of the US economy",
       subtitle = "Each series rescaled to its own range",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Data: ggplot2::economics_long")
```

## Pairing light fills with main outlines

The `"light"` palette has the same colours as `"main"` in the same order, so
the two pair up. Use light fills for large areas and main colours for edges.

```{r density}
ggplot(mpg, aes(hwy, fill = drv, colour = drv)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.75, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_jac_d(palette = "light",
                   labels = c("Four-wheel", "Front", "Rear")) +
  scale_colour_jac_d(labels = c("Four-wheel", "Front", "Rear")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = NULL, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(title = "Front-wheel drive goes further",
       subtitle = "Distribution of highway fuel economy",
       x = "Highway miles per gallon", y = NULL,
       caption = "Data: ggplot2::mpg")
```

## Ordered categories

For categories with a natural order, use the sequential palette. Its
lightest colour is almost white, which works for filled areas but
disappears as small points on a white background. Take a few extra colours
with `jac_pal()` and drop the lightest. Darker means a better cut.

```{r scatter-ordered}
set.seed(2611)
gems <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 2500), ]

ggplot(gems, aes(carat, price, colour = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 1.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = jac_pal("seq", n = 6)[-1]) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0("$", x / 1000, "k")) +
  labs(title = "Bigger diamonds, higher prices",
       subtitle = "2,500 diamonds sampled at random, coloured by cut quality",
       x = "Carat", y = NULL, caption = "Data: ggplot2::diamonds") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1,
                               override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1)))
```

## Continuous values

`scale_fill_jac_c()` uses the sequential palette by default, running from
pale for low values to deep violet for high ones.

```{r heatmap}
ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster(interpolate = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_jac_c(guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Old Faithful keeps two rhythms",
       subtitle = "Density of eruptions by length and waiting time",
       x = "Waiting time (minutes)", y = "Eruption (minutes)",
       caption = "Data: ggplot2::faithfuld")
```

## Diverging values around zero

Correlations run from -1 to 1, with 0 meaning no relationship. Set
`midpoint = 0` and fixed `limits` so that zero always gets the neutral
centre colour.

```{r correlation, fig.height = 5.6}
vars <- c("mpg", "cyl", "disp", "hp", "drat", "wt", "qsec")
r <- cor(mtcars[vars])
cors <- data.frame(
  x = factor(rep(vars, each = length(vars)), levels = vars),
  y = factor(rep(vars, times = length(vars)), levels = rev(vars)),
  r = as.vector(r)
)

ggplot(cors, aes(x, y, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r),
                colour = abs(r) > 0.6), size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_jac_c(palette = "div", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1),
                   name = "Correlation") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey20"),
                      guide = "none") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "What goes with fuel economy?",
       subtitle = "Pairwise correlations between car characteristics",
       x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Data: datasets::mtcars") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"))
```

## Base R graphics

jacarandr only returns hex codes, so its palettes work without ggplot2 too.

```{r base-contour, fig.height = 5.2, eval = TRUE}
old <- par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
image(volcano, col = jac_pal("seq", n = 100), axes = FALSE, asp = 61 / 87,
      useRaster = TRUE,
      main = "Maunga Whau volcano, in jacaranda")
contour(volcano, add = TRUE, drawlabels = FALSE, col = "white", lwd = 0.4,
        nlevels = 12)
par(old)
```
